questions.stem: Which input pattern stops when the user enters -1?
questions.solution: A sentinel value ends the loop.

questions.stem: Which statement immediately exits a loop?
questions.solution: break terminates the nearest loop or switch.

questions.stem: Which item is NOT a programming paradigm?
questions.solution: Debugging is an activity, not a programming paradigm.

questions.stem: Which declaration creates a floating-point variable named price?
questions.solution: float is used for real numbers.

questions.stem: Which part of a for loop is executed after each iteration?
questions.solution: The update expression runs after each iteration.

questions.stem: Which phase of the program development life cycle defines what the program must do?
questions.solution: Analysis establishes the requirements before design and coding.

questions.stem: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.solution: do...while tests the condition after the body.
% is the modulus operator and returns the remainder.

questions.stem: What is the index of the first element of a C++ array?
Which values can a bool variable hold?
questions.solution: A bool holds true or false.

questions.stem: This question tests algorithms and programming errors.

parts.answer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem. Pseudocode is a structured English-like description of an algorithm.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correct definition.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain THREE types of programming errors and give one example of each.
parts.answer: Syntax error: missing semicolon. Runtime error: division by zero. Logic error: using < instead of <= in a condition.
parts.solution: Award 0.5 mark for each type and 0.5 mark for a valid example.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A concert charges RM15 for ages 0-12, RM25 for ages 13-17 and RM40 for ages 18 and above. A negative age is invalid.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Start -> read age -> if age < 0 display invalid; else if age <= 12 price = 15; else if age <= 17 price = 25; else price = 40 -> display price -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, all ranges, output and flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Use if/else if with the three ranges and an invalid-age branch.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, range conditions, assignment and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests declarations, constants and expressions.

parts.text: Write C++ declarations for: an integer age, a double price, a constant discount rate of 0.10 and a character grade.
parts.answer: int age; double price; const double DISCOUNT = 0.10; char grade;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct types, names and const initialisation.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write C++ statements to read age and price, calculate price after discount, and display the result.
parts.answer: cin >> age >> price; price = price - price * DISCOUNT; cout << price;
parts.solution: Award marks for input, discount expression and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and state the output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Rewrite the segment using a do...while loop that sums only values greater than 5.
parts.answer: int i=0,s=0; do { if(a[i]>5) s+=a[i]; i++; } while(i<5); cout<<s;
parts.solution: Award marks for do...while, condition, filter and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A sports club stores sport names and medal counts in parallel arrays.

parts.text: Declare two parallel arrays for five sports and initialise them with suitable values.
parts.solution: Award marks for both declarations, correct sizes and related indices.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment to display each sport with its medals, then calculate the total and average medals.
parts.answer: Loop i=0..4 to display sports[i] and medals[i], accumulate total, average = double(total)/5.
parts.solution: Award marks for paired display, total, average and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A cafe sells three items: coffee RM8.50, tea RM6.00 and juice RM9.50. A 10% discount is given when the subtotal is at least RM50.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.

parts.text: Write a complete C++ program that reads the item code and quantity, calculates the subtotal and discount, and displays a formatted receipt with the item name, quantity, subtotal, discount and amount to pay.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.

questions.stem: A bookstore records up to five books. Each book has a title, price and quantity in stock.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.

parts.text: Define a struct Book. Write a complete C++ program that reads the records, calculates the total inventory value, and displays the title of the most expensive book.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for struct definition, 4 for input, 4 for inventory value, 3 for most expensive and 1 for output.
